method: Inspected all 14 contact sheets (front, threequarter, left, right rows; 8 phases, 16 for get-up) and enlarged native 480x480 frames for key phases of every exercise; cross-checked geometry.json clearances and read figure.ts, hand-model.ts, kettlebell-model.ts and contracts.json. Could not observe playback: timing, pacing and loop smoothness not directly observed (geometry reports sub-mm loop seams). Views between the four sampled angles and phases between samples were not inspected.

kb-swing.summary: Clearest clip in the set: hinge, hip drive and chest-height float read in every view; the dark bell hangs convincingly below long arms and differentiates it from the deadlift.

defects.issue: Forearms graze the thighs (-5 mm) at the bottom of the backswing; hands and bell merge into one blob between the knees in the front view
defects.fix: Widen the backswing path by ~1 cm so forearms clear the thighs; optional minor

kb-deadlift.summary: Floor start, stand and floor reset are readable and the bell visibly touches the floor between the feet; arm/thigh interpenetration near lockout is the remaining visible defect.

defects.issue: Forearms sink ~2 cm into the thighs as the figure stands (upper arms -1 cm at 0.95); arms and thighs fuse into one silhouette in side views
defects.fix: Move the hang path or shoulders forward slightly so arms rest on, not inside, the thigh surface

defects.issue: At the floor position hands, handle and knees cluster tightly; grip reads only as two white blobs over the handle
defects.fix: Slightly widen stance/knee track or lower camera emphasis so the handle and both hands separate

goblet-squat.summary: Goblet hold at the chest is obvious in all views, depth and upright torso read clearly, and feet stay planted.

defects.issue: Upper arms touch the thighs at depth (-4.5 mm), minor merge of elbow and knee silhouettes
defects.fix: Tuck elbows a few mm inside the knees or reduce depth slightly

kb-reverse-lunge.summary: Step-back, rear-knee drop and alternation are clear in three-quarter and side views; goblet hold stays readable.

defects.issue: The rear leg hides behind the front leg, so the lunge reads as a shallow one-leg squat from the front
defects.fix: Acceptable for a sagittal lunge; optionally angle the stepping line a few degrees so the rear shin shows from the front

kb-side-lunge.summary: Wide stance and weight shift to each side are clear from front and three-quarter; nonworking leg stays long.

defects.issue: From pure side views the lateral shift is invisible and the pose reads as a goblet squat
defects.fix: Inherent to a frontal-plane move; no change required, but default the camera to front/three-quarter for this exercise

kb-upright-row.summary: Bell travels close to the body to chest height with elbows leading; distinct from clean and curl in all views.

defects.issue: At the top the elbows rise above shoulder level and the forearms/hands form a tight cluster over the upper chest, partly obscuring the bell handle
defects.fix: Stop the top a little lower (elbows at or just below shoulder height) so hands and handle stay separate from the shoulders

kb-bent-row.summary: Hinge and two-hand pull read in side and three-quarter views, but the pull amplitude is small and the front view barely changes.

defects.issue: Bell only rises from knee to lower-thigh height; front view frames 0 and 0.5 look nearly identical and the clip is easily confused with a hinge hold/deadlift
defects.fix: Increase row travel so the bell reaches the lower ribs/navel and the elbows clearly pass the torso line

defects.issue: Bell sits ~3 cm from the thigh at the top, visually overlapping it in side view
defects.fix: Draw the bell path slightly further from the thighs as it rises

kb-side-bend.summary: The lateral bend is visible from the front and three-quarter, but the bell does not ride the outer thigh, the free hand leaves the hip, and side views show almost nothing.

defects.issue: Right hand drifts off the hip and floats beside the waist at the deepest bend, breaking the 'hand on hip' cue
defects.fix: Pin the right hand to the iliac crest throughout the bend

defects.issue: Bell hangs 5-10 cm outside the thigh and tilts off plumb, so it neither slides down the outer thigh nor reads as a hanging weight
defects.fix: Keep the bell plumb under the handle and against the outer thigh as it slides down

defects.issue: Side views show only a standing figure with the bell over the thigh; the bend is not legible
defects.fix: Increase bend amplitude slightly and default the camera to front/three-quarter for this exercise

kb-curl.summary: The elbow-flexion arc is visible, but at the top the bell sticks out horizontally in front of the fist, defying gravity, and at the bottom it passes into the thigh.

defects.issue: Bell body is cantilevered forward of the fist with the handle horizontal, at hand height; the weight looks glued on and weightless, and the forearm stops short of full flexion
defects.fix: Hang the bell body below the handle (or rest it against the forearm for a bottoms-down curl) and bring the forearm to full flexion near the shoulder

defects.issue: Bell interpenetrates the front of the thigh by ~2 cm at the bottom
defects.fix: Offset the hang position so the bell clears the thigh by a few mm

kb-halo.summary: The circle around the head reads in three-quarter and side views and the horns grip is plausible, but the front view loses the bell behind the head and the action is small in a full-body frame.

defects.issue: Bell disappears completely behind the head; only raised elbows are visible, so the rear pass is unreadable from the front
defects.fix: Keep the bell slightly lower/offset behind the head so part of the body shows, or apply the contract's upper-body crop so the loop fills the frame

defects.issue: Full-body framing leaves the bell circle occupying a small area at 480 px; hands and horns are hard to resolve
defects.fix: Use the upper-body three-quarter crop the contract specifies

kb-clean.summary: Backswing, hip drive and rack are all present and distinct from swing/snatch, but the rack does not show the bell resting on the forearm and the arm clips the thigh.

defects.issue: In the rack the bell body projects horizontally in front of the fist at chin height instead of resting on the outside of the forearm; it reads as floating
defects.fix: Orient the bell so the handle runs diagonally through the palm and the body hangs below/behind the handle against the back of the forearm (body centre below the handle, axis tilted), keeping the grip ring on the handle

defects.issue: Upper arm passes ~1 cm into the thigh in the backswing
defects.fix: Keep the working arm on the thigh surface during the hinge

kb-press.summary: Rack-to-lockout path is clear and differentiated, but the bell is drawn lying sideways at both rack and lockout, undermining weight and the 'back of forearm' cue.

defects.issue: Bell body sits beside the fist at handle height with the handle horizontal, as if the bell were lying on its side in mid-air; it does not rest on the back of the forearm and reads weightless
defects.fix: Orient the bell so the handle runs diagonally through the palm and the body hangs below/behind the handle against the back of the forearm (body centre below the handle, axis tilted), keeping the grip ring on the handle

defects.issue: Rack bell sits forward of the fist on a horizontal handle rather than against the forearm
defects.fix: Orient the bell so the handle runs diagonally through the palm and the body hangs below/behind the handle against the back of the forearm (body centre below the handle, axis tilted), keeping the grip ring on the handle

kb-snatch.summary: Lockout, drop, backswing and high pull are distinct from the clean and swing, but the lockout bell floats sideways and the bell grazes the thighs in the backswing.

defects.issue: Bell body sits beside the fist at handle height with the handle horizontal, as if the bell were lying on its side in mid-air; it does not rest on the back of the forearm and reads weightless
defects.fix: Orient the bell so the handle runs diagonally through the palm and the body hangs below/behind the handle against the back of the forearm (body centre below the handle, axis tilted), keeping the grip ring on the handle

defects.issue: Bell intersects the far thigh (-4.6 mm) and the working upper arm the near thigh (-7 mm) in the backswing
defects.fix: Widen the backswing path so bell and arm pass between the thighs

kb-getup.summary: Major stages (post, bridge, sweep, half-kneel, stand) are recognisable in side views, but the loop never shows the supine start, the bell floats sideways overhead throughout, and front/three-quarter transitions tangle.

defects.issue: Loop starts already propped on the hand; there is no lying-down frame, so the start of the get-up is not shown
defects.fix: Include the supine start with the bell pressed and floor contact of back and shoulders

defects.issue: Bell body sits beside the fist at handle height with the handle horizontal, as if the bell were lying on its side in mid-air; it does not rest on the back of the forearm and reads weightless; the bell is the viewer's focus in this exercise
defects.fix: Orient the bell so the handle runs diagonally through the palm and the body hangs below/behind the handle against the back of the forearm (body centre below the handle, axis tilted), keeping the grip ring on the handle

defects.issue: During the bridge and sweep the head drops sideways and the support arm, far leg and torso overlap into an unreadable knot; support-hand contact is hard to see
defects.fix: Adjust the sweep path or the default camera so the posted hand, knee and planted foot separate in silhouette
